Hereditary alveolar proteinosis causes intraalveolar surfactant accumulation and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
Spastic paraplegia and extrapyramidal dysfunction define a neurologic disorder.

Isolated intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
Lysosomal oligosaccharide storage disorder; intellectual disability occurs in 80–99% and ataxia in 30–79%. Hearing, skeletal and ocular damage are occasional.
Structural skeletal myopathy; reduced FVC and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness without established lung or gut damage. Aortic coarctation occurs in 20%.
Umbrella category defined by inherited cardiovascular abnormalities; other organ involvement varies by subtype.
Tricuspid valve leaflet prolapse causes valvular insufficiency.
Primary melanoma arising in leptomeningeal melanocytes within the central nervous system.
Autoimmune endocardial and valvular vegetations; associated lupus and embolic cerebrovascular disease are separately diagnosed conditions.
Chronic inflammatory polyradiculoneuropathy affects peripheral nerves and nerve roots, typically through immune-mediated injury.
Immune-mediated lichenoid skin inflammation distributed along Blaschko lines; other lichen planus sites are not established for this subtype.
Benign melanocytic tumor arising in eyelid skin; both eyelid and cutaneous sites are explicit.
Autonomic nervous system failure causes the defining loss of blood pressure regulation on standing.
Malignancy of renal-associated adipose tissue, classified as kidney sarcoma; perirenal fat origin does not establish skin or locomotor involvement.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with spastic paraplegia; distal muscle wasting in 4/4 and skin ulcers in 80–99%. Osteomyelitis occurs in only 25%.
Inherited podocyte disease causes nephrotic syndrome and progressive kidney failure; secondary lipid abnormalities do not establish another organ disease.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow defined by the specified chromosomal inversion.
RDH12-associated retinal degeneration causes severe visual impairment; optic disc changes remain within the ocular axis.
A lymphoblastic leukemia affecting hematopoietic cells and marrow; no additional common organ damage is established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural deafness with vestibular dysfunction; both hearing and vestibular function belong to the otologic axis.
Neuropathy, intellectual disability and deafness define the syndrome; muscle wasting occurs in 80–99%, with pes cavus in 30–79%. Respiratory insufficiency is <30%.
